title: Born in a prison
hookLine: Krishna is born in a prison cell, and his mother asks God to hide his glory
carry: god comes small enough to hold
tomorrow: one small word, 'but', splits two schools. what does it say?

lines: FOUR ARMS IN A PRISON CELL.
cards: Well-known people do it all the time: a cap pulled low, sunglasses, a plain gray hoodie, so they can get through an airport like anyone else. The Bhagavata Purana has a stranger version.
A baby is born at midnight in a prison cell in Mathura. For a moment he shows his parents who he really is: four arms, holding the conch, the discus, the mace and the lotus.
And his mother, Devaki, asks him to put it away. Hide that, please. So why would a mother ask God to look less like God?

teach.h: SHE ASKS HIM TO HIDE IT.
teach.b: Because Kamsa is coming. Devaki and her husband Vasudeva are in chains, and the king, her own brother, has sworn to kill this child.
In the Purana, Devaki praises him, and then the praise turns into a plea: I'm afraid; take that form back. And he does. Before their eyes he becomes an ordinary newborn.

teach.h: THE CHAINS SLIP, THE DOORS OPEN.
teach.b: Then the chains slip off, the guards fall asleep where they stand, and the doors open by themselves.

teach.h: ACROSS THE YAMUNA IN THE RAIN.
teach.b: Vasudeva lifts the baby and walks out into the rain, to the Yamuna river, and the river makes way for them.

On the far side, in Gokula, he lays the boy beside Yashoda, who has just given birth to a daughter, and carries the girl back to the cell. By morning, Krishna is a cowherd family's son. So here's the puzzle, solved.
The hidden form isn't a trick. It's how this god chooses to come: small enough to hold. That's a big teaching in Krishna bhakti, loving devotion.
Many devotees don't only bow to Krishna as Lord of all; they love him the way Yashoda did, as a child to feed and dress and rock to sleep. Teachers call it vatsalya, a parent's love.

It's why so many Hindu home shrines keep a baby Krishna, often called Bal Gopal or Laddu Gopal, and why on Janmashtami families stay up to midnight and rock a little cradle. A God you can only bow to is far away.
A God you can hold is close.

how: Many Hindu homes keep a baby Krishna (Bal Gopal or Laddu Gopal) on the shrine and offer him food; at Janmashtami some fast until midnight, the hour of his birth in the story, and rock a small cradle.

o: the river spirit who parted the Yamuna's water
Vishnu, born in a prison and raised by cowherds
the king of Mathura who feared a prophecy

games.q: one night, many hands — tap the pairs.
p: asks him to hide his four-armed form
her brother, sworn to kill the child
carries the baby through the rain
raises him as her own son

s: Krishna was born in a palace, as a prince
he was born in Kamsa's prison, with his parents in chains.
his mother asked him to hide his four-armed form
Devaki, afraid of Kamsa, asked; he became an ordinary baby.
Vasudeva left the baby with strangers by chance
he laid him beside Yashoda, newly a mother, and carried her daughter back.

games.q: at Janmashtami your aunt hands you the string to rock baby Krishna's cradle. a friend whispers: isn't that a bit silly, for God? what's the answer?
o: it's bhakti: Krishna came as a baby so people could love him up close.
it's only for kids; grown-ups worship the warrior Krishna instead.
it means Krishna was weak at first and became God later.
games.why: in the Bhagavata, God hides his four arms at Devaki's plea and is carried out as a baby. devotees love him like Yashoda did: vatsalya, a parent's love.

practice: If you keep a shrine, offer Krishna something small, the way families do for Bal Gopal: a sweet, a piece of fruit, a flower. If you don't pray, hold one small thing you'd give a child you love.
Either way, sit with it in front of you, breathing slow and quiet, and let the gift stay small for the whole sit.

wordCard.voice: Krishna: Vishnu born in Kamsa's prison, carried across the Yamuna by night, and raised in Gokula as a cowherd family's son.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: Krishna, the child born in Kamsa's prison.

carryVoice: Keep this: God comes small enough to hold. Krishna let himself be carried through the rain. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.3 (Krishna's birth; the four-armed form; Devaki's request; the crossing of the Yamuna; the exchange with Yashoda's daughter)
